title: Session priming: marginal latency vs dollar scan (lab notes)
body:
Goal:
Quickly characterize the marginal impact of session priming (sending short context up-front) on p50/p90 latency and dollars-per-1k-tokens across three deployment profiles. This is exploratory lab output for product/optimize to decide whether to recommend explicit primer sizing in SDKs and console presets.

Motivation / hypothesis:
- Many clients send a 64-512 token primer (system instructions + few-shot examples).
- Primer increases per-request compute but improves cache hit rates for subsequent turns; amortization depends on session length.
- We hypothesize: small primers (~64 tokens) increase p50 by a small % but reduce p90 for multi-turn sessions via higher KV cache reuse.

Environment / setup:
- Date: experiments run 2026-02-11 -> 2026-02-14 in perf-lab (eu-west1).
- Model: open-llama-13b (baseline), quant-4 (4-bit static Q), distilled-7b (fast path).
- Runtime paths: hosted-fastpath (multiplex + small batch), dedicated-tiling (reserved GPUs, tiling enabled), private-edge-small (1 GPU, low memory).
- Workload: synthetic conversational sessions (turn length distribution):
  - short: 2 turns (user->assistant) avg tokens/session = 120
  - medium: 6 turns avg tokens/session = 480
  - long: 20 turns avg tokens/session = 2500
- Primers tested: none, 64 tokens, 256 tokens, 512 tokens added at session start. Primer content = stable few-shot template (same across runs).
- Measurement: p50/p90 latency (ms) per request, end-to-end cost estimate ($/1k tokens) using our internal cost model (GPU-second * infra rate + infra overhead).
- Notes: network jitter filtered by taking runs with median throughput; cold start mitigated by 30s warmup.

Raw aggregated table (median of 3 runs each):

Config | Primer | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | $ / 1k tokens | note
------------------------------------------------------------------
Baseline: open-13b hosted-fastpath
none   | 0      | 86       | 312      | 1.98          | short-session heavy p90s
64     | 108    | 274      | 2.12          | p50 +25% p90 -12%
256    | 154    | 248      | 2.48          | p50 +79% p90 -21%
512    | 212    | 290      | 2.95          | p50 +146% p90 -7% (diminishing)

Quant-4: open-13b quantized dedicated-tiling
none   | 72     | 256      | 1.30          | lower $ but similar p90 shape
64     | 94     | 220      | 1.40          | p50 +30% p90 -14%
256    | 128    | 198      | 1.62          | good p90 drop for medium/long
512    | 182    | 210      | 1.98          | marginal returns beyond 256

Distilled-7b: private-edge-small
none   | 48     | 192      | 3.40          | cheaper latency but higher infra rate on small edge
64     | 66     | 168      | 3.68          | p90 improves, p50 modest increase
256    | 98     | 150      | 4.20          | p90 wins on long sessions but $ rises fast
512    | 145    | 144      | 5.05          | p90 plateaus, cost skyrockets

Quick ASCII visualization (p90 trend by primer size, normalized):

p90 (normalized; 1.0 = none)
open-13b-hosted:  1.00  0.88  0.79  0.93
quant-4-dedicated:1.00  0.86  0.77  0.82
distill-7b-edge:  1.00  0.87  0.78  0.75

Interpretation / takeaways:
- Small primer (64 tokens) consistently reduces p90 across model/runtime combos (~10-15%) at the expense of a modest p50 increase (~20-35%). That matches the hypothesis: priming helps tail via reuse.
- Medium primer (~256 tokens) often gives the best p90/dollar tradeoff for medium and long sessions especially on quantized dedicated setups (p90 -20% while $ increases only ~25%).
- Large primers (512 tokens) generally increase both p50 and cost significantly and show diminishing p90 returns — in some hosted configs p90 regresses due to batching/tiling inefficiencies introduced by larger prefix.
- Distilled-7b on private-edge: strong p90 improvements but cost per token on edge hardware is high; primer advice should be different for edge customers (restrict primer size or recommend dedicated).

Operational notes (why p90 improves):
- Primer populates KV-cache entries and reduces future decode overhead for repeated token patterns in assistant responses.
- For tiling/quant paths, the primer helps better kernel selection (longer contiguous sequences allow faster decode kernels).
- For hosted-multiplex, larger primers can push requests into a different batching lane (longer sequences => larger batch decisions) which occasionally hurts p50 for short sessions.

Risk/unknowns / TODOs:
- We used a single primer template. Real-world primers vary in token redundancy; need corpus sweep across customer primers (ENG-4523).
- Interaction with function-calling / tool outputs not tested — primers that encourage tool calls may change latency profile.
- Need longer-run economics: how primers affect overall platform QPS and slot allocation in multiplexed pools.
- Verify behavior for multimodal inputs (images + text primers).
- Confirm quant-4 results with more seed runs and different quant libs (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/912 touches quant codepaths).

Practical recommendations (initial):
- SDK: add a "primer_hint" boolean and an example preset for "short-primer" (<=64) and "medium-primer" (<=256). Recommend medium only for customers with average session length > 10 turns.
- Console: add a one-line tooltip on model config pages: "priming can reduce tail latency for multi-turn sessions; primer sizes >256 tokens may increase cost and p50".
- Default: keep SDK default = no primer; provide an opt-in wizard for customers migrating from single-turn to multi-turn flows.

Next experiments (30d plan):
1) Customer primer sweep: instrument anonymized primer length distribution from top 50 tenants and re-run representative primers (privacy-preserving sampling). Owner: Maya. (JIRA-ENG-4621)
2) Function-calling + primer interaction matrix (short/long tool outputs). Owner: Jonah.
3) Multiplex slot impact: simulate increased primer adoption on multiplex pools to observe slot churn and effective $/1k token at scale. Owner: Rafael.

Notes to self / rough todo checklist:
- [ ] Add script to automatically convert primer text -> token histogram; share with product for primer-size UX thresholds.
- [ ] Hook quant-4 run logs into bench dashboard (trace ids in PR 912).
- [ ] Draft a short console tooltip copy for design review (product/ux).

Appendix: micro-case examples (single-session trace excerpts)
- short session (hosted, 64 primer)
  request 0: primer 64 tokens injected (time 0)
  request 1: user turn 1 (30 tokens) -> p50=110ms p90=290ms (assistant tokens 120)
  request 2: user turn 2 (20 tokens) -> p50=48ms p90=78ms (assistant tokens 50) -- demonstrates amortization

- long session (dedicated quant-4, 256 primer)
  request 0: primer 256 -> p50=128ms p90=198ms
  request 1..n: repeated assistant generation shows 35-60% lower decode-time per turn after primer (observed in traces)

Questions for next sync with product/optimize:
- Is recommending a "medium primer" for >10-turn sessions productizable without confusing users? (need UX/words)
- Should we add a cost-estimate preview in console that shows projected $/1k tokens for primer sizes?

Links / refs:
- Quant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/912
- Related ticket: JIRA-ENG-4523 (primer telemetry)
- Draft SDK change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/234 (primer_hint param)

-- end --
